mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation expectations rise sharply (CPIAUCSL y/y > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 y/y change < -2% AND HOUST y/y change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing decline are reversed within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months, in the absence of offsetting wage growth (PAYEMS flat or falling), indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that depress earnings and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS y/y change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the unemployment rate reverts below 6% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO y/y change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in industrial production reverses within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp, unexpected increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL y/y > 4%) that is not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS flat) signals a credibility or policy-lag risk, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL y/y > 4% AND FEDFUNDS y/y change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% over six consecutive months, with no corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE ≤ 4%), signals robust consumer demand that supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS y/y change > 0.5% for six consecutive months AND UNRATE ≤ 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or real retail sales decelerate below 0.2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS y/y change rising by at least 0.5pp quarter-over-quarter) without a corresponding rise in wage growth (CPIAUCSL y/y ≤ 3%) indicates labor supply expansion, which boosts corporate margins and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS y/y change slope > 0.5pp q/q AND CPIAUCSL y/y ≤ 3%
regime_hint: labor market loosening with stable prices
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or wage inflation exceeds 3% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) of more than 10% year-over-year, in the absence of a concurrent decline in unemployment (UNRATE ≤ 4%), signals a housing-specific demand shock that depresses construction-related equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or housing starts rebound by more than 5% in the following month.
